messages:
sara_support: customer reports intermittent 504s + duplicate billing logs when callers cancel contexts aggressively. using go-sdk v0.10.1 with custom http.Client. stack: customer sends request, cancels ctx, SDK retries -> server sees two in-flight requests.
chen_eng: thanks, can you paste minimal repro? do we know if they set Transport.DisableKeepAlives or custom RoundTripper? :thinking_face:
sara_support: repro snippet they gave: ```ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 100*time.Millisecond); defer cancel(); req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, \"POST\", url, bytes.NewBuffer(payload)); client.Do(req) // client is sdk.httpClient with Transport pooling``` They see short timeouts then server logs duplicate request IDs.
omar_sre: sounds like cancellation races where the client cancels but transport reuses the connection and the retry uses same TCP stream before the previous request fully drained. Go's net/http can re-use if body not closed. are they reading/closing resp.Body on cancel path?
lisa_cse: customer says they cancel before body read because they only need headers on timeout. they relied on SDK to close body + not retry on cancelled contexts.
chen_eng: SDK older behavior: we did an internal retry wrapper that doesn't check ctx.Err() before starting the retry if previous Do returned an error that looked retryable (timeout). combined with http.Transport re-use this can cause server to receive overlapping requests. new SDK patch adds a ctx check and sets Transport.DisableKeepAlives for the retry attempt.
sara_support: suggested interim mitigations to customer: 1) set Transport.DisableKeepAlives=true 2) ensure you call resp.Body.Close() in all paths 3) upgrade to go-sdk >= v0.10.3 which includes the ctx pre-check.
omar_sre: also try setting http.Transport.IdleConnTimeout lower so connections don't linger. but main fix is to avoid starting a new request after ctx cancelled.
chen_eng: patch notes I'll share: \"Go SDK v0.10.3: always check context error before scheduling retry; ensure Do called with new request bound to current ctx; on retry we set Request.Close=true if underlying Transport supports it to avoid connection reuse during retry window.\"
sara_support: customer also worried about billing duplicates — suggested we add a header X-Redwood-Idempotency to detect duplicates server-side and to reduce billing risk while they upgrade.
lisa_cse: added a short repro test for our CI: ```func TestCancelThenRetry(t *testing.T){srv := httptest.NewServer(func(w http.ResponseWriter,r *http.Request){time.Sleep(50*time.Millisecond); fmt.Fprintln(w, \"ok\")}); defer srv.Close(); c := newSDKClientWithTransport(&http.Transport{DisableKeepAlives:false}); ctx,cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Millisecond); defer cancel(); _, err := c.DoWithRetries(ctx, srv.URL, nil); if err == nil {t.Fatalf(\"expected err\")}}``` flags show flakiness pre-patch, stable post-patch.
chen_eng: @deploybot can we schedule a patch release tomorrow AM and add a release note calling out cancellation/retry behavior? :hammer:
deploybot: scheduled release v0.10.3 tomorrow 09:30 PT. changelog entry created.
sara_support: customer will try the workaround and we will follow up. marking as high-priority until they confirm. :eyes:
